body.x: Recently in the press and the IT community, tongues have been wagging about LG Electronics’ smartphone Optimus G. The phone is the bold new product designed when Gu Bon-mu, chairman of the LG Group, ordered various companies in the LG group to combine their expertise, and it boasts the finest performance of any smartphone on the market today. While every aspect of the phone is excellent, there are two that really stand out. These are the 13-megapixel camera module and the uni-body touch screen called the G2 Touch Hybrid. These two parts are available for your perusal at LG Innotek’s booth at KES 2012.

The camera module that LG Innotek designed for the Optimus G wins points in the three areas of ultra high-resolution, ultra-small size, and ultra-thin design. At 13 megapixels, the photo resolution is high enough for printing extra large photos.

In order to achieve the highest possible screen quality, LG Innotek selected optimized optical parts, and it used color matching between the camera and the display to express colors more accurately than normal cameras.

To keep the phone from getting too thick while still equipping it with a high-resolution camera module, LG Innotek implemented some of its own newly designed technology. With the goal of making the world’s smallest device, the company used sensors with pixels that are 1.1㎛ in size (㎛ is a micrometer, about 1/100 th of the thickness of a single hair).

The camera also features a lens that offers a wide lens while remaining thin, employing high-precision packaging technology that assembles parts carefully and precisely in order to reduce the size even further.

While this is not the first product to have a camera that exceeds 10 megapixels, most products with such specifications have been specialized products for photographers. The only smartphones not specialized for photography to be equipped with a camera that is 10 megapixels or higher are the Pantech Vega S5 and the Optimus G.

“To keep the phone from getting thicker while still packing in 13 megapixels - the highest resolution of any smartphone camera module released to date - we had to use a variety of cutting-edge technologies,” said Mun Hyeong-cheol, managing director of the second optical solutions team at LG Innotek. “We were able to create an ultra-thin camera by implementing technology including 1.1㎛ sensors, an ultra-thin lens, and high-accuracy packaging.”

The G2 Touch Hybrid touch screen on the phone combines the strengthened glass on the front, the touch sensors, and the display panel into one thin component. It replaces the ITO (indium tin oxide) film with ITO-coated cover glass while eliminating as much of the space as possible between the touch sensors, the LCD panel, and the strengthened glass. As a result, designers were able to reduce the width of the G2 Touch Hybrid screen to around 70% of standard display panels. This is one of the keys to the slim design of the Optimus G. The smartphone was a joint production by LG Innotek and LG Display.
